'''Sunčica Čanić''' is a [[Croatian Americans|Croatian-American]] mathematician, the Hugh Roy and Lillie Cranz Cullen Distinguished Professor of Mathematics and Director of the Center for Mathematical Biosciences at the [[University of Houston]],<ref>{{citation |title=Newly Named Cullen Professor Uses Mathematics to Benefit Heart Research |url=https://uh.edu/nsm/news-events/stories/2008/0910_canic.php |access-date=19 January 2022 |publisher=University of Houston |date=10 September 2008}}</ref><ref name="cv">{{citation|url=http://www.math.uh.edu/~canic/CANICcv.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Sunčica Čanić|accessdate=2015-10-13}}</ref> and Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. She is known for her work in mathematically modeling the human [[cardiovascular system]] and medical devices for it.<ref name="bionews"/>

==Education and career==
Čanić earned bachelor's and master's degrees in mathematics in 1984 and 1986 from the [[University of Zagreb]]. She completed her Ph.D. in 1992 in [[applied mathematics]] from [[Stony Brook University]], under the joint supervision of Bradley J. Plohr and [[James Glimm]]. She became an assistant professor at [[Iowa State University]] in 1992, and moved to the University of Houston in 1998. She became the Cullen Distinguished Professor in 2008,<ref name="cv"/> and Professor of Mathematics at U.C. Berkeley in 2018. She has most recently taught the undergraduate multivariable and vector calculus course at UC Berkeley. She is also a member of the board of governors of the [[Institute for Mathematics and its Applications]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.ima.umn.edu/governance/Suncica.Canic.html|title=Suncica Canic|work=Board of Governors|publisher=[[Institute for Mathematics and its Applications]]|accessdate=2015-10-13}}.</ref>

==Contributions==
Čanić's research has involved the computational simulation of the [[stent]]s used to treat arterial clogging. By finding ways of simplifying computer models of stents from hundreds of thousands of nodes to only 400 nodes, she was able to make these simulations much more efficient, and used them to design improved stents that reduce clotting and scar formation.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.nsf.gov/mobile/discoveries/disc_summ.jsp?cntn_id=117540&org=ERE|first=Stephanie|last=Dutchen|date=August 26, 2010|title=Scientists use math to build better stents|publisher=[[National Science Foundation]]|work=Behind the Scenes}}.</ref> She has also led the development of a procedure for heart valve replacement surgery that is less traumatic than open-heart surgery.<ref name="bionews">{{citation|url=http://bionews-tx.com/news/2014/08/26/uh-mathematicians-work-to-become-basis-for-open-heart-surgery-alternative/|title=UH mathematician's work to become basis for open-heart surgery alternative|date=August 26, 2014|first=Anna|last=Tan|work=BioNews Texas |accessdate=2015-10-13}}.</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2014 she was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] "for contributions to the modeling and analysis of [[partial differential equation]]s motivated by applications in the life sciences."<ref>{{citation|url=http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2014|title=SIAM Fellows: Class of 2014|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]|accessdate=2015-10-13}}.</ref>
She was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the 2020 Class, for "contributions to partial differential equations, and for mathematical modeling of fluid-structure interactions that has influenced the design of medical devices".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2020 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=2019-11-03}}</ref> She was honored as the 2024 [[AWM-SIAM Sonia Kovalevsky Lecture|AWM-SIAM Sonia Kovalevsky Lecturer]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2024 Kovalevsky Lecture |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/kovalevsky-lectures/kovalevsky-lecture-2024/ |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]] |language=en-US}}</ref>
